reference: GNU coreutils split(1), run under system Bash with the harness reference PATH; parity compares status, stdout, and complete private fixture trees including bytes and modes. Bash type/help metadata contracts use Bash builtins and the generated short-help description pinned in config/bash-loadables.list.
coverage: Default stdin input and xaa prefix naming
Line chunk boundaries, a one-character suffix, and an unterminated final record
Byte chunk boundaries over NUL and high-bit bytes, including an exact multiple with no empty trailing piece
The 1k byte-size suffix at the 1024-byte boundary
Decimal KB versus binary KiB units, implicit unit counts, and overflowing byte sizes
Two redirected stdin invocations in one shell
Truncation of an existing piece and umask-derived modes for a new piece
Bash builtin type and generated short-help metadata
G68: --filter=COMMAND, with FILE exported, early-closing filters, and filter exit/signal statuses.
Guest compatibility pass 5 (G74/G83): pass5-long-lines-bytes, pass5-number-elide-hex, pass5-line-bytes-and-separator, pass5-long-diagnostics.
Guest compatibility pass 6 (G90): GNU diagnostic wording for operand and usage errors.
Pass 8 (G121): -a 0 is the default suffix length, -a 8 and longer are accepted, an overlong length is rejected.
exclusions: This is focused coverage, not the full GNU split option surface; numeric line/byte splitting and common suffix behavior are covered, while options such as --elide-empty-files are outside the documented builtin interface.
No host/device paths, write-failure devices, or input aliasing cases are used.

cases.purpose: With no input or prefix operand, split reads stdin and creates the default xaa piece.
cases.script: printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' | split

cases.purpose: Split five records into two-line pieces, use a one-character suffix, and preserve the final unterminated record.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
last' > input; split -l 2 -a 1 input part_

cases.purpose: Byte splitting must preserve NUL and high-bit bytes and must not create an empty piece when the input length is an exact multiple of the chunk size.
cases.script: printf 'A\000BC\377D' > input; split -b 3 input binary_

cases.purpose: The 1k byte-size suffix denotes 1024 bytes: a 1025-byte fixture should produce one full piece and one one-byte piece.
cases.script: printf '%1025s' '' > input; split -b 1k input kilo_

cases.purpose: Two split invocations in one shell consume separate redirected stdin streams, first by lines and then by bytes.
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
c
' > first; printf '\000xyz' > second; split -l 2 - first_ < first; split -b 2 - second_ < second

cases.purpose: An existing first piece is truncated rather than appended, its existing mode remains, and a newly created second piece follows the active umask.
cases.script:
printf 'fresh
next
' > input; umask 077; printf 'old data that must be truncated
' > itemaa; split -l 1 input item

cases.purpose: If the first output name is an existing directory, split reports a write/open failure and leaves the directory and input fixture intact.
cases.script: printf 'content\n' > input; mkdir pieceaa; split -l 1 input piece

cases.purpose: A zero line count is invalid; GNU status and candidate status are both asserted against the reference, and no output piece should be created.
cases.script: printf 'unchanged\n' > input; split -l 0 input bad_

cases.purpose: Decimal and IEC units produce different chunk boundaries and work in repeated invocations.
cases.script: printf '%2050s' '' > input; split -b 1KB input decimal_; split -b1KiB input binary_; split -b KB input implicit_

cases.purpose: Byte sizes beyond the integer limit remain valid and preserve the entire input.
cases.script: printf 'large size, small input' > input; split -b 18446744073709551616 input integer_; split -b 1QB input unit_

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata identifies the statically provided split command as a builtin, independently of PATH lookup.
cases.script: type -t split

cases.purpose: Bash short help reports the supported split command synopsis.
cases.script: help -s split
cases.stdout: split: split [-l N | -b SIZE | -C SIZE | -n CHUNKS] [-a SUFLEN] [-d|-x] [-e] [-t SEP] [-u] [--verbose] [--additional-suffix=S] [--filter=COMMAND] [INPUT [PREFIX]]

cases.purpose: -d and bare --numeric-suffixes give decimal names from 00, -x hexadecimal ones, --hex-suffixes=FROM starts in hex, and --additional-suffix is appended after the generated suffix (guest pass 2 G35).
cases.script:
printf 0123 > f; printf a > g
split -b 2 -d f p
split -b 1 --numeric-suffixes f n
split -b 1 -x f h
split -b 1 --hex-suffixes=10 f r
split -b 1 -d -a 1 --additional-suffix=.txt f t
split --additional-suffix .x g q
split -b 1 -d --numeric-suffixes=3 f m
ls

cases.purpose: An --additional-suffix containing '/' is rejected with status 1 and creates nothing.
cases.script: printf a > g; rc=0; split --additional-suffix=a/b g p || rc=$?; echo rc=$rc; ls

cases.purpose: G68: --filter=COMMAND and --filter COMMAND pipe each piece to $SHELL -c COMMAND (here /bin/sh) with FILE set to the piece name; no piece file is created by split itself.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 > in
split -l 3 --filter='while IFS= read -r l; do printf "%s:%s\n" "$FILE" "$l"; done' in
split -b 5 --filter 'n=0; while IFS= read -r l; do n=$((n+1)); done; printf "%s %s\n" "$FILE" $n' in
split -n l/2 -d --additional-suffix=.txt --filter='read -r first; printf "%s<%s>\n" "$FILE" "$first" > "$FILE.out"' in p_
ls

cases.purpose: G68: a filter that stops reading early is not an error; a failing filter's exit or signal becomes split's status with GNU's message; --filter rejects -n K/N and a missing COMMAND.
cases.script:
i=0; while [ $i -lt 20000 ]; do i=$((i+1)); echo "line $i"; done > big
split -l 5000 --filter='read -r l; printf "%s %s\n" "$FILE" "$l"' big
rc=0; split -l 2 --filter='exit 3' big || rc=$?; echo exit-rc=$rc
rc=0; split -l 2 --filter='kill -TERM $$' big || rc=$?; echo signal-rc=$rc
rc=0; split -n 1/3 --filter=true big || rc=$?; echo chunk-rc=$rc
rc=0; split --filter || rc=$?; echo missing-rc=$rc

cases.purpose: G74: --lines, --bytes, --suffix-length, --numeric-suffixes=FROM, --additional-suffix and --verbose.
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3
4
5
' > in; split --lines=2 in L; split --bytes 4 --suffix-length=3 in B; split --lines 2 --numeric-suffixes=5 --additional-suffix=.t --verbose in N; for f in L* B* N*; do printf '%s:' "$f"; cat "$f"; done

cases.purpose: G74: --number=N, --elide-empty-files and --hex-suffixes.
cases.script: printf 'ab' > in; split --number=4 --elide-empty-files in E; split --number 3 --hex-suffixes in H; for f in E* H*; do printf '%s:' "$f"; cat "$f"; echo; done

cases.purpose: G74: --line-bytes packs whole lines (an unterminated final record included) and -t/--separator splits records on another byte.
cases.script:
printf 'aa
bbbb
cc
ddddddd
e' > in; split --line-bytes=5 in C; printf 'a,b,c,d' > s; split --separator=, -l 2 s S; for f in C* S*; do printf '%s:' "$f"; cat "$f"; echo; done

cases.purpose: G74: ambiguous and unknown long options and a multi-character separator print GNU's diagnostics.
cases.script: { split --s 2 /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { split --bogus || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { split -t ab /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'

cases.purpose: G90: GNU split's "cannot open 'NAME' for reading", a read error naming the input ('-' for standard input) and the extra-operand diagnostic with its Try line; no output piece is created.
cases.script:
mkdir d
printf 'x\n' > f
{ split nosuch || echo rc=$?; } 2>err
{ split 'a b' || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
{ split d || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
{ split < d || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
{ split f p extra || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //' err >&2
rm err

cases.purpose: split -l x prints "split: invalid number of lines: 'x'" with no usage line, -b "invalid number of bytes", -C GNU 9.7's "invalid number of lines", -a "invalid suffix length"; status 1 (guest pass 7, G105).
cases.script:
s() { local rc=0; eval "$1" 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
s 'split -l x </dev/null'
s 'split -l 0 </dev/null'
s 'split -l '"'"''"'"' </dev/null'
s 'split -l 1x </dev/null'
s 'split --lines=x </dev/null'
s 'split -b x </dev/null'
s 'split -b 0 </dev/null'
s 'split -C x </dev/null'
s 'split -a x </dev/null'
s 'split --bogus </dev/null'

cases.purpose: G121: -a 0 means the default length.
cases.script:
rc=0
seq 3 | split -l1 -a 0 || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"
rc=0
ls x* || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"

cases.purpose: G121: -a 8 is accepted.
cases.script:
rc=0
seq 3 | split -l1 -a 8 || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"
rc=0
ls x* || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"

cases.purpose: G121: a suffix length too large for the type is rejected.
